newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Labour supports European arms code.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Labour supports European arms code.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour party said on Thursday it would support the idea of a Europe-wide code of conduct on arms sales if it took power.

Foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook laid out an eight-point pledge to guarantee a "responsible" arms trade on the first anniversary of the Scott Report, an official report into illegal British arms exports to Iraq before the 1991 Gulf War.
Cook said he believed Britain had the right to maintain its competitive edge in the arms market but it must also accept its responsibility to ensure the market is properly regulated.
It could not, however, do this in isolation, Cook said.

"Labour will press for a European Register of Arms Exports which will provide at a European level the information that Britain will make available in the annual report (on UK strategic exports)," Cook said.
"Labour will work for the introduction of a European Code of Conduct setting high common standards to govern arms exports from all European Union member states."

Saferworld, a pressure group covering the arms industry, said a European code of conduct would help prevent arms exports to countries which abuse human rights, regions of instability, military aggressors and dictatorial regimes.

"A European code of conduct would ensure that commercial gain would never again override concerns for international security and human rights in arms export decisions," Saferworld said in a statement.
Labour is far ahead of the ruling Conservatives in opinion polls before an election which must be held by May 22. REUTER
